comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C33-C36 regarding ADGRA3 expression patterns, regulation by HFD/CL, and correlation with UCP1. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED without concerns about the expression data or correlation analysis.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C94-C98 regarding human cell and primary culture experiments. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers specifically noting these in vitro experiments avoid the tissue selectivity issues present in the in vivo work.

Perfect agreement on claims C115-C116 regarding off-target expression and tissue selectivity limitations. Both evaluations acknowledge these as valid concerns, with OpenEval viewing them as appropriate caveats and peer reviewers citing them as a central limitation undermining in vivo interpretations.

Strong agreement on claims C13, C71-C78 regarding the Gs-PKA-CREB signaling mechanism. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers explicitly stating this mechanism is 'well-established' and accepting the co-IP and pathway analysis without challenge.

Significant disagreement on claims C5-C6, C50-C60 regarding in vivo knockdown phenotypes. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with adequate controls and sample sizes, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN due to tissue selectivity concerns with nanoparticle-mediated knockdown affecting multiple tissues beyond adipose.

Significant disagreement on claims C7-C8, C61-C70 regarding in vivo overexpression phenotypes. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with robust gain-of-function effects, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN due to the same tissue selectivity limitations affecting interpretation of metabolic improvements.

Disagreement on claims C39-C44 regarding in vitro knockdown effects. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by multiple complementary assays, while peer reviewers group these with in vivo knockdown data (C5-C6, C50-C60) and express UNCERTAIN evaluation due to broader tissue selectivity concerns, though the in vitro data itself is less problematic.

Disagreement on claims C45-C49 regarding in vitro overexpression effects. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as complementary gain-of-function data, while peer reviewers group these with in vivo overexpression data (C7-C8, C61-C70) and rate UNCERTAIN due to tissue selectivity concerns in the broader experimental approach.

Disagreement on claims C11-C12, C85-C93 regarding in vivo hesperetin efficacy and ADGRA3-dependency. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with appropriate four-group design demonstrating dependency, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN because the nanoparticle-mediated knockdown used to test dependency has tissue selectivity issues.

Partial disagreement on claims C10, C79-C84 regarding hesperetin as ADGRA3 agonist and in vitro validation. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with computational screening and functional validation, while peer reviewers acknowledge the findings but express UNCERTAIN evaluation when considering the broader context including in vivo dependency experiments (C85-C93).

Agreement on claims C4, C32, C112 regarding ADGRA3 identification and characterization. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader claim set (C4, C28-C32, C37-C38, C112) while peer review focuses on subset, but both accept the core identification and expression findings.

Agreement on claims C37-C38 regarding ADGRA3 cellular localization in adipocytes. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED as part of characterization data, with no disputes about the localization findings.

OpenEval evaluated claims C1-C2, C20 regarding rationale for seeking ADRB3 alternatives and found them SUPPORTED by citations and expression data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/rationale claims.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background claims C15-C27, C99-C111, C114 and found them SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims establishing scientific rationale.

OpenEval evaluated claim C113 regarding ADGRA3 expression relative to ADRB2 and found it SUPPORTED by expression data and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this comparative expression claim.

Peer reviewers evaluated claim C3 (not explicitly listed in OpenEval results) as part of the key finding that ADGRA3 is a valuable target for thermogenic activity. This appears to be a summary claim that OpenEval may have addressed through multiple other result groups rather than as a standalone evaluation.
